sales_hooks: AMD MI325X has 256GB HBM — highest per-GPU capacity on the market, making AMD the natural choice for memory-constrained LLM inference. This is a positioning story memory suppliers should amplify.
Samsung is AMD's primary HBM3 supplier for MI300X — a unique customer relationship that Samsung's memory marketing team should be actively managing vs SK Hynix's NVIDIA dominance.
AMD datacenter GPU revenue +36% YoY — the 'alternative to NVIDIA' demand is real; hyperscalers are dual-sourcing AMD to reduce NVIDIA dependency, which diversifies HBM demand.
MI350 (3nm, HBM3e 288GB) samples H1 2026 — qualification timing for Micron HBM3e is a live opportunity. Micron could break AMD's SK Hynix dependency at this transition.

competitive_position.vs_nvidia: Price/performance competitive for inference; CUDA ecosystem remains a 10-year moat for NVIDIA
competitive_position.vs_intel: AMD far ahead on AI GPU; Intel Gaudi largely irrelevant at hyperscaler scale
competitive_position.hbm_relationship: Samsung primary for MI300X; SK Hynix growing share in MI325X/MI350

scm_engagement.scm_role: Designs competing AI GPUs (Instinct MI series) to NVIDIA. Also the #1 supplier of x86 server CPUs (EPYC) that serve as the host CPU in AI servers alongside NVIDIA or AMD GPUs. Every AI server has an EPYC CPU; AMD earns from both the CPU and GPU tier.

lead_time.description: AMD GPU ship-out → tokens served ≈ 8 months. Longer than NVIDIA because AMD ROCm software stack requires more porting work (less mature than CUDA), adding 2-3 months for model optimization.
lead_time.bottleneck: ROCm software stack maturity — vLLM/PyTorch support adds 6-8 weeks vs NVIDIA CUDA
